statement: A design card that names an external command as its cryptographic primitive must be checked against the repository's own capability boundary before the design is treated as fixed. The signed-issuance card specified ssh-keygen -Y sign and -Y verify inside the CLI while also requiring src/__tests__/offline-boundary-guard.ts to pass unchanged; that guard permits node:child_process in exactly one file, so both invocations were unavailable. Two constraints of one card collided and only one was a hard rule. Re-derive the primitive inside the boundary rather than widening it: SSHSIG verification is implementable in pure node:crypto and was cross-checked against real ssh-keygen output on accept and on reject, while signing moved out of process entirely, so the tool never reads private key material and verification needs no OpenSSH installed. Read the guard before writing the module, and state the deviation loudly rather than quietly adding an allowlist entry.

anchors.summary: PR #331 adds pure node:crypto SSHSIG verification and cross-checks it against OpenSSH acceptance and rejection.

statement: A parser for a security-policy file must treat a field it did not interpret as disqualifying, never as absent. An OpenSSH allowed-signers line can carry options — cert-authority, namespaces="...", validity windows — that narrow or change what a key authorizes. A parser that reads the principal, key type and key while skipping the option field silently widens what verifies, and the widening is invisible because the happy path still passes. The issuance verifier keeps uninterpreted option text on the parsed entry and refuses to match against any line that carries one, so an unrecognised restriction fails closed; the same reasoning makes an empty or key-less signers file report 'signed by an unlisted key' rather than skipping the check, because 'nobody may sign' must never read the same as 'anybody may'.

anchors.summary: PR #331 disqualifies uninterpreted signer options and refuses an empty or key-less signer list.
